text: Capabilities and interfaces Operation Rust CLI Python Backend RCSP pricing and enumeration Yes Through routing solves Low-level Solver Core Rust Routing root relaxation Yes Default vrptw / cvrp mode pybaldes.solve_root Clp Branch-and-price tree Yes --tree Not exposed Clp Complete enumerated node MIP Yes, opt-in --tree --enumerated-mip Not exposed Clp + HiGHS Generic mixed-integer master solve highs::solve_integer Not exposed directly Not exposed HiGHS The routing tree currently models one pricing network. A network is aseparate routing subproblem, such as a vehicle type or depot. Forward andbackward labeling within one graph do not create multiple networks.Ryan–Foster branching works with one network. Packing-set assignment rows aresupported, but useful fractional assignment branching requires multiplenetworks; see Branching. Root Optimal means the LP relaxation converged. A feasiblerestricted-column solution supplies an incumbent; its objective alone doesnot prove a lower bound for the full routing problem.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
text: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle Documentation index · Branching ·Enumerated MIP The Rust tree solves a routing set-partitioning master with one pricing graph.It requires nonnegative arc costs and unique public arc IDs. The base rows area fleet upper bound and one equality per customer; the tree validates thisstructure before searching.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Run a tree

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Node processing
text: Node processing The search selects a node by its lower bound and evaluates it within theremaining global budget. Its main steps are: Construct the root master, or fork the solved parent and append the child'sconstraints. Run column generation, pricing, cut rounds, and enabled fixing/enumeration. Share valid elementary routes with the incumbent heuristic and other nodes. Search restricted columns for a feasible integer solution; optionally runHiGHS over a complete enumerated universe. Close the node when its certified bound meets the incumbent gap, or selecta branching candidate and create children. Strong trials and diving useisolated evaluations. Time limits are cooperative across solver operations. A backend call canfinish after its requested budget. Limits preserve bounds for unfinished nodes.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: What a child inherits
text: What a child inherits State Child handling Clp master Deep-copy model, basis, solution, scaling, and simplex state Branch and cut rows Preserve physical rows and coefficient mappings; append new branch rows Existing route columns Retain coefficients and upper bounds; retire routes outside the new domain Pricing graph Carry bucket preparation, fixed bucket arcs, NG state, options, and adaptive state Labels Rebuild for the child's duals and active branch resources Enumeration Retain/filter routes where compatible and preserve branch-distinct arc paths Sibling state Own independent mutable models and pricing state When enumeration changes the master to full-memory cut coefficients, existingcolumns are updated as well as new ones. Reusing limited-memory coefficientsfor only part of the enumerated master would change the model.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Root snapshots and manual inheritance
text: Root snapshots and manual inheritance Set RootOptions::capture_state = true to retain a solved NodeSnapshot inRootOutput::snapshot. The tree arranges snapshot capture for its own nodes.Manual callers use root::inherit_branches(parent, additional_branches, options)for typed constraints, or root::inherit for arc-flow tuples. Supply only theadditional branches; the parent already contains its ancestor rows.To retain the child's snapshot for another generation, enable capture on thatsolve too. The snapshot exposes branch_depth(), active_cuts(), andenumerated_routes(). A route count alone does not establish completeness;the enumerated-MIP adapter separately checks the completion flag.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Incumbents, proofs, and status
text: Incumbents, proofs, and status Source Supplies an incumbent? Certifies the routing lower bound? Validated elementary route solution Yes No, by its objective alone Restricted-column integer heuristic Yes, after validation No Exact node pricing When the resulting routes form an integer witness Yes, through its certified bound Heuristic strong trial or dive Can find a witness No proof for the original node Complete enumerated HiGHS MIP Yes, after validation Only within saved enumeration coverage and for proved outcomes A cost-only --upper-bound can assist root fixing, but the tree needs actualfeasible routes before accepting an incumbent. It does not invent a solutionfrom the supplied number. Optimal means the configured numerical gap is closed. TimeLimit,NodeLimit, and Incomplete retain unfinished-node bounds. Check whether afinite incumbent and routes are present before treating a limited run as asolution. JSON encodes nonfinite numbers as null. The restricted-column heuristic uses TreeOptions::mip_node_limit andmip_time_limit; CLI --mip-nodes budgets that heuristic. Optional HiGHS nodeMIP has separate controls and counters; see Enumerated MIP.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Limits and validation
text: Limits and validation The tree does not yet provide multiple pricing networks, generic nodepreprocessing, or cut callbacks during the integer solve. Python exposesroot solving; use Rust or the CLI for the tree. Node snapshots and inheritance Tree driver Lifecycle tests: fixing carry, sibling isolation,full-memory updates, grandchildren, and failed setup Tree tests: exhaustive route universes, limits,feasible witnesses, and branch/cut preservation cargo test --features clp --test node_lifecycle --test branch_price

title: Routing branching
heading: Routing branching
text: Routing branching Documentation index · Tree lifecycle The tree branches on aggregate route quantities. Each child receives a typedconstraint, inherited master rows, and a compatible pricing domain. Thestandard routing model uses customer vertices as packing sets and enforcesunit customer coverage with equality rows.

title: Routing branching
heading: Choosing families
text:
Choosing families CLI mode Candidate families, in priority order --branching native (default) Vehicle count, packing-set assignment, Ryan–Foster, arc flow --branching vehicles Vehicle count, then arc-flow fallback --branching ryan-foster Ryan–Foster, then arc-flow fallback --branching arc Arc flow The selector uses the first enabled family with fractional candidates. Withinan applicable family it orders candidates by closeness of the fractional partto 0.5, with stable ties. Phased strong branching then evaluates candidateswhen enabled. These are adapter priorities, not a combined ranking across allfamilies. cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 10 --tree \
  --branching ryan-foster --time 60
 Rust configures the family flags through TreeOptions::branching, whose typeis BranchingOptions. Arc flow remains the fallback when all flags are false.

title: Routing branching
heading: Number of vehicles
text:
Number of vehicles Let v be the sum of LP values of nonempty routes in the selected network.For fractional v, the children enforce: down: number of nonempty routes <= floor(v)
up:   number of nonempty routes >= ceil(v)
 Pricing receives this row through nonempty-route return arcs to the sink.The split-depot source-to-sink arc contributes zero to this branch. Theoriginal fleet upper bound remains in the master.

title: Routing branching
heading: Ryan–Foster
text: Ryan–Foster For customers i and j, let w(i,j) be the sum of LP route values for routesvisiting both customers. When 0 < w(i,j) < 1, the children require: Child Allowed routes Apart A route can visit at most one of the pair Together A route visits both customers or neither Both children work with a single pricing network. The together conditionapplies to each route, rather than merely requiring both customers somewherein the final solution. Binary resources enforce the rule during labeling and bidirectional joins.Retained enumeration is filtered by the same rule. Existing NG routes thatrepeat a pair endpoint are retired from the child master. A violation row alsokeeps inherited and newly added master columns consistent with the branch. An apart constraint consumes one binary resource; a together constraintconsumes three. The current representation holds 512 resources. Candidategeneration skips already-branched pairs and falls back to arc flow when itcannot reserve resources for both Ryan–Foster children.

title: Routing branching
heading: Packing-set assignment
text: Packing-set assignment This family branches on assigning a customer packing set to a particularpricing network. If its fractional assignment to network k is y, thechildren enforce assignment to that network as zero or at least one.For example, in a heterogeneous fleet this could decide whether customer 7uses the small-vehicle network. The current tree has one network. Its customer equality rows already fixeach assignment to one. Assignment constraints can be constructed and enforced,but the normal single-network LP has no fractional assignment candidate. Anunassigned child for a mandatory customer is infeasible. Useful assignment branching requires multiple route families/networks,network-specific costs and resources, and master columns carrying the networkidentity. Setting a graph ID alone does not add that modeling support.

title: Routing branching
heading: Directed arc flow
text: Directed arc flow For a directed arc with fractional LP usage f, the children enforce flow atmost floor(f) or at least ceil(f). Route coefficients count traversals ofthe arc; branch duals also reach pricing through that arc. BranchConstraint::ArcFlow::arc takes the arc's position inproblem.graph.arcs, while Route::arcs stores public arc IDs. UseRootProblem::arc_position(id) to convert an ID to a position.

title: Routing branching
heading: Strong branching and diving
text: Strong branching and diving Strong branching is enabled by default. Its three phases retain up to 100restricted-LP candidates, price three survivors heuristically, then evaluateone with exact pricing. StrongBranchingOptions exposes the phase and timebudgets. Disable it with --no-strong-branching. Strong round-up diving uses isolated route-fixing trials and depth,discrepancy, node, and time limits. Disable it with --no-diving.Heuristic trial objectives and dive bounds cannot certify the original node.See Tree lifecycle for bound and incumbent handling.

title: Routing branching
heading: Implementation and checks
text: Implementation and checks Typed constraints and route coefficients Candidate generation and history checks Ryan–Foster pricing resources Branching tests: both children, resource limits,fresh versus inherited models, and pricing with active cuts Tree tests: exhaustive small instances, strongtrials, diving, and incomplete-bound handling cargo test --features clp --test branching --test branch_price

title: Routing cuts
heading: Routing cuts
text: Routing cuts Documentation index · BALDES options ·Source layout A cut must have consistent coefficients in the master, pricing, retainedroutes, and descendants. The root adapter installs cut rows and dual effects;node snapshots retain active rows and the pricing state needed to use them.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Available families
text: Available families Family Purpose Rust root configuration CLI / Python Limited-memory rank-one Strengthen the customer-cover relaxation with_rank_one_cuts() --rank1 / rank_one_cuts=True Rounded capacity Enforce capacity-derived subset inequalities with_capacity_cuts(config) --capacity-cuts / capacity_cuts=True Kohl 2-path Use time-window feasibility to strengthen capacity subsets Capacity config with time windows --two-path-cuts / two_path_cuts=True Strong k-path Separate route-count inequalities on customer sets with_kpath_cuts(config) or with_native_kpath_cuts(config) Rust API Route-load knapsack Separate inequalities on integer resource loads with_knapsack_cuts(config) Rust API All routing root integrations require clp. HiGHS is needed only for theoptional enumerated integer solve. Cut configuration does not enable thatsolve automatically.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Start with capacity and rank-one cuts

title: Routing cuts
heading: Strong k-path adapters
text: Strong k-path adapters KPathCutConfig::new(demands, capacity) is the routing convenience adapter.Its demand vector uses depot index 0 and customer indices 1..n; the splitsink is n + 1. with_time_windows supplies optional time-window data. NativeKPathCutConfig accepts explicit graphs, graph IDs, packing/coveringset incidence, and demands in the original zero-based set order without adepot entry. Use it when the convenience adapter does not represent the inputmapping. with_kpath_cuts and with_native_kpath_cuts select alternativeadapters; the most recently selected one replaces the other. Graph IDs, set IDs, and pricing vertex indices have different roles. Keepthose mappings explicit when registering cuts. Full-memory enumeration andlimited-memory pricing can use different coefficient state; the adapterupdates the master when switching modes.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Route-load knapsack and resource IDs
text: Route-load knapsack and resource IDs KnapsackCutConfig::new(rows) takes integer resource rows fromcuts::knapsack::KnapsackRow. Separation uses route resource loads, andpricing must charge the same load-dependent contribution. Ordinary arc-onlycosts are insufficient for this family. KnapsackCutConfig::with_resource_indices(map) maps resource IDs in thoserows to coordinates in the pricing solver. An empty map uses identitymapping. For example, an input resource identified as 7 can map to solvercoordinate 1. This changes the coordinate lookup, while preserving resourceIDs in the cut associations. The mapping must remain valid through pricing,enumeration, and child inheritance. Keep rows integer-scaled according to their model semantics. The resourcemap is not a unit conversion. See the mapped-resource and load-dependentpricing cases in the integration tests forcomplete fixtures.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Configuration boundaries
text: Configuration boundaries Named BALDES options do not create model data. Enabling capacity separationstill requires demands and vehicle capacity; setting a knapsack mode stillrequires resource rows. Explicit capacity enablement and per-round overridesare applied after inherited cut state is installed. Knapsack constructionoverrides do not reconfigure an existing inherited separator. See BALDES options for supported values and setter errors.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Pricing, enumeration, and integer solving
text: Pricing, enumeration, and integer solving Separation creates rows and registers their pricing state. Pricing incorporates active cut duals while constructing routes. Complete elementary enumeration uses full-memory coefficients, includingupdates to route columns already in the master. Child snapshots preserve active rows and cut state. The optionalHiGHS solve rebuilds full-memory route columns againstevery active physical row and omits artificial columns. The cut registry and coefficient logic live under src/cuts.Root scheduling and row remapping live in theroot controller.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Validation

Validation cargo test --features clp --test capacity_root --test kpath_knapsack
cargo test --features clp,highs --test highs_mip
 The suites cover small exhaustive validity checks, separation violations,bidirectional pricing, enumeration repricing, mapped resource IDs, timewindows, and inherited cut rows. The HiGHS tests exercise complete nodemasters across the existing cut-family configurations.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
text: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS Documentation index · Tree lifecycle ·BALDES options BALDES can solve a complete enumerated node master with HiGHS, while keepingClp for column generation. The integer solve uses a separate HiGHS instanceand leaves the source LP, its solution/basis, and sibling snapshots untouched.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Controls and API

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Enumeration gate
text: Enumeration gate The route universe must be complete and its route count must not exceed theconfigured threshold. Equality and a completed empty universe are accepted.BALDESmaxNumOfEnumSolutionsForMIP defaults to 10,000;BALDESmaxNumOfEnumSolsForEndOfNodeMIP defaults to zero and is raised to at leastthe normal threshold. An incomplete universe never passes the gate. Settingonly the end-of-node option to zero does not disable the solve, because the normal threshold stillraises it. The gate counts retained enumerated routes before adding anypreviously priced elementary witness routes to the integer model.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Preserving node semantics
text: Preserving node semantics The snapshot adapter copies the current physical row order, including baserows, inherited typed branches, and every active capacity, rank-one, strongk-path and route-load knapsack row. It rebuilds route columns using currentbase/branch coefficients and full-memory cut coefficients. It preservesexisting route upper bounds, including zero bounds. Artificial columns areomitted, so finite artificial penalties cannot masquerade as feasibility. Previously priced elementary routes are independently reconstructed andvalidated before being retained as possible witnesses. Enumeration can haveremoved a previously found incumbent route at its cutoff; retaining validatedold routes avoids losing that witness. Every added route still receives everybranch and active cut row. EnumeratedMipOutput::coverage_cutoff records the incumbent under which theuniverse was restricted (or the existing 1e12 fallback). A proof about thismatrix alone cannot exclude solutions above that cutoff. The tree uses at mostthe minimum of the proved MIP bound and that coverage cutoff. It records avalidated routing witness before closing a gap. Without a witness, a finitecoverage cutoff cannot establish global infeasibility.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Outcomes
text: Outcomes Outcome Interpretation Optimal HiGHS proved the integer model optimal and supplied a validated improving witness Infeasible HiGHS proved the transferred integer model infeasible; node interpretation still depends on enumeration coverage ObjectiveCutoff The proved integer optimum does not improve the caller's cutoff; no feasible incumbent is invented from that cutoff TimeLimit / NodeLimit Unfinished solve; any validated improving incumbent is retained, but the tree does not treat the limit as a proof Incomplete Other or ambiguous statuses, including unbounded-or-infeasible and unusable witnesses; no node-closing proof A finite objective_cutoff filters improving witnesses after solving; it isnot installed as a HiGHS search cutoff. The source model is copied beforesolving, so a supplied cutoff never substitutes for a feasible incumbent.Coefficients with nonzero magnitude at most 1e-12 are rejected to avoidsilent matrix changes in HiGHS. HiGHS relative and absolute MIP gaps are set to zero. Its model status isretained in MipOutput::solver_status, with solution, dual bound, node count,simplex iterations, and elapsed time. Tree JSON adds enumerated_mip_calls andenumerated_mip_nodes; its existing mip_nodes includes this work too.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Validation and remaining gaps
text:
Validation and remaining gaps tests/highs_mip.rs covers generic Clp/HiGHS model transfer, source isolation,rows and upper bounds, mixed integrality, infeasibility, cutoffs, zero budgets,50 independent exhaustive integer comparisons, threshold boundaries and timereserve, and complete snapshot solves across all five existing cut-familyconfigurations. Child tests enforce vehicle count, together/apart, arc-flow andassignment rows and then re-solve the parent to check isolation. Tree and CLItests exercise opt-in MIP, disabled enumeration, exhausted budgets, and missingbackend support. Run the MIP and command-line checks with both backends: cargo test --features clp,highs --test highs_mip --test cli
 See Build and validation for the full feature matrix and Pythonchecks. The implementation lives in theHiGHS model transfer,snapshot adapter, andtree integration. BALDES currently runs the optional solve after node evaluation. A handoffinside column generation, new cut separation during integer solving, andmultiple pricing networks remain outside this implementation. Active rowsare all retained.

title: BALDES pricing options
heading: BALDES pricing options
text: BALDES pricing options Documentation index · Cuts ·Enumerated MIP The public option names start with BALDES. The standard build exposes39 supported pricing options. Builds with both clp and highs exposetwo additional enumerated-MIP controls. Each option below has a consumer;some apply only to a particular operation or a configured cut family. Rust exposes the supported metadata through OPTION_TABLE and availabilitythrough Options::support(name). Python lists supported names withSolver.option_names() and reports scope with Solver.option_support(name).The C option-count/name functions use the same supported table. Listings arespecific to the features enabled in the build. Use Solver::set_option to update a live solver. Options itself is a validatedoption-value container; changing solver.options directly does not synchronizecontrols, phase schedules or engine state. Failed live-solver setters preservethe prior option values, controls, phases and prepared engine.

title: BALDES pricing options
heading: Configuration and runtime overrides
text: Configuration and runtime overrides BALDESlabelDominanceStrategy accepts 0 or 1 and reaches labeling throughSolver::dominance_mode. The dedicated C strategy setter uses the samepath, so its value agrees with the named option getter. Full-label fixingstill selects its required dominance behavior. BALDESuseCapacityCuts and BALDEScapCutsMaxNumPerRound override an explicitlyconfigured root capacity separator and apply after inherited cut state isinstalled. Omitting an override preserves the configuration or parent'ssettings. Enabling the option alone does not create demands or a separator. BALDEScapacityCutsSeparator selects the available built-in separator fornonzero values. Value 0 requests external CVRPSEP, which is unavailable andis rejected explicitly. Positive capacity cut limits are required.

title: BALDES pricing options
heading: Examples and verification

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Dual-price stabilization
text: Dual-price stabilization Documentation index · Tree lifecycle Column generation can repeatedly produce similar master duals and columns.BALDES optionally smooths the dual point sent to pricing, using a storedcenter and bounded retries when smoothed pricing finds no fresh columns.It is enabled by default in column_generation::Options. The implementation isDualPriceSmoothing, integrated by thecolumn-generation loop. The sections belowdescribe the implemented update and retry rules.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Smoothing weight
text:
Smoothing weight For raw master duals raw, stored center, and an outward point outward: pricing[i] = (1 - effective_alpha) * outward[i]
           + effective_alpha * center[i]
 By default outward = raw. Larger alpha means more weight on the center.At alpha zero pricing uses the outward point; at alpha one it uses the center.Reducing alpha moves pricing back toward the current master duals. After interpolation, a positive dual on a LessEqual row or a negative dualon a GreaterEqual row is set to zero when its magnitude exceeds theconfigured tolerance. Equality rows have no such sign restriction.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Parameters
text: Parameters These are Rust master::stabilization::Parameters, configured throughRootOptions::cg.smoothing or directly in column_generation::Options.They are separate from the named BALDES pricing options. Parameter Default Behavior alpha_factor 1.0 Below 1: use that base alpha and the linear retry rule; otherwise adapt alpha dynamically initial_alpha 0.5 Initial base alpha for the dynamic mode beta_factor 0.0 Zero: use raw outward point; positive: enable the directional construction below max_updates 10 Maximum smoothed retry updates before returning to raw duals min_gap 0.0 Minimum accepted gap, using the comparison tolerance max_gap 0.0 Maximum accepted gap; nonpositive disables the upper gate minimum_stage 0 Minimum stage accepted by after_master tolerance 1e-6 General comparison and sign-correction tolerance The current column-generation caller passes stage 0 to after_master andpasses the actual pricing phase in feedback. Raising minimum_stage abovezero therefore disables activation in that caller. Its gap argument is themaster LP value minus the current finite bound, or zero when no finite boundis available.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Lifecycle
text: Lifecycle Method Effect restart_schedule(phase) Reset base/effective alpha, retry count, active flag, and center phase; retain the stored center/bound vectors after_master(...) Apply a pending center, store raw duals/senses, reset retries, and activate smoothing if the stage/gap/alpha gates allow it after_pricing(feedback) Consider a center update, adjust base alpha, and decide whether pricing should retry after_iteration() Clear the moved-center marker and return active pricing to raw duals remap_rows(map) Compact dual, center, sense, and pending-center vectors after row removal The first master iteration uses raw duals. Cut/enumeration transitions restartthe schedule; row cleanup applies the row map. Removing columns alone doesnot change row coordinates and does not require a center remap.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Pricing retries and alpha updates
text:
Pricing retries and alpha updates Feedback includes the fresh negative-column count, a subgradient vector,Lagrangian value, and pricing phase. In the column-generation driver, thesubgradient starts at the row RHS and subtracts multiplicity times the bestacceptable column's coefficients when its reduced-cost magnitude passes thenumeric test. On the first pricing pass in dynamic mode (alpha_factor >= 1): if no fresh negative columns or angle > 1e-12:
    alpha -= 0.1
else if angle < -1e-12 and alpha is below the near-one gate:
    alpha += 0.1 * (1 - alpha)
 The angle threshold is 1e-12, independently of Parameters::tolerance.The near-one gate includes the general tolerance and a relative margin.Updating base alpha affects subsequent master iterations; retries update thecurrent effective alpha separately. If fresh negative columns exist, or smoothing is inactive, after_pricingreturns false and stops retrying. Otherwise it increments misprices and uses: dynamic mode: effective_alpha = 2 * effective_alpha - 1
fixed-base mode: effective_alpha = 1 - misprices * (1 - alpha)
 It republishes a smoothed point only while the retry count is at mostmax_updates and effective alpha exceeds the tolerance. When either gatefails, it deactivates smoothing and requests a final retry at raw duals.“Fixed” describes the base alpha, not an unchanging effective retry weight.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Center updates
text:
Center updates A nonfinite Lagrangian value is ignored. If the current center phase is lessthan or equal to the feedback phase, a finite center bound is replaced onlywhen the new value improves it beyond tolerance. A lower-numbered feedbackphase can reset the center phase and accept a different bound without thatsame improvement requirement. The accepted pricing point and feedback subgradient become a pendingcenter, installed by the next after_master call. Consequently the storedcenter bound is not unconditionally monotone across phase changes. The angle helper computes: toward = pricing - center
angle = dot(toward, feedback_subgradient)
      / (norm(toward) * norm(feedback_subgradient))
 The division is unguarded. A zero denominator may yield NaN; comparisonswith it then fail. This behavior differs from forcing an angle of zero.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Optional directional construction
text:
Optional directional construction With positive beta_factor, let d = raw - center, l = norm(d), and gbe the stored center subgradient. A negligible l returns raw duals.For beta_factor == 1, beta is the cosine between d and g; a negligiblesubgradient also returns raw duals. Otherwise the configured beta is used.Beta is clamped to [0, 1] before constructing: outward = center + (1 - beta) * d - beta * l * g / norm(g)
 A negligible subgradient contributes zero to its directional term. When theconstructed step has norm above 1e-12, it is rescaled to length l. Thischanges the outward point before the alpha interpolation.

heading: Configure or disable

title: Source layout
heading: Source layout
text: Source layout Documentation index · Tree lifecycle · Cuts The Rust crate groups code by solver responsibility. Directory mod.rs filesprovide entry points and public exports; implementation files hold the routines.Existing Rust import paths and C symbols remain available. Directory Responsibility src/api/ C ABI handles, graph construction, options, pricing, fixing, relaxation, solution access, and statistics src/core/ Shared errors, logging, and solver options src/cuts/ Cut registry and cut-family modules src/graph/ Graph representation, buckets, NG preparation, relaxation, and symmetry src/labeling/ Labeling engine, label storage, and route pool src/enumeration/ Full-memory elementary enumeration src/pricing/ Stateful pricing workflow, branching resources, fixing, and NG updates src/master/ Restricted master, column generation, stabilization, branching constraints, root driver, and tree src/hgs/ Hybrid genetic search: individuals, split, local search, genetic operators, population, and driver src/vrptw/ Solomon/CVRPLIB instances, parsing, graph construction, and optional root adapter src/bin/ Command-line application

title: Source layout
heading: Cuts
text: Cuts cuts/mod.rs exports the registry and its public types. capacity/, knapsack/,kpath/, and rank_one/ own their respective cut families. shared/ owns commoncut-state, graph, and container helpers. Compatibility exports retainpaths such as cuts::state and cuts::separation.

title: Source layout
heading: Master and tree
text: Master and tree master/root/mod.rs owns solved-node snapshots, mutable root state, and solveor inheritance entry points. problem.rs owns rows and route coefficients;options.rs owns root and cut-family configuration; controller.rs ownscolumn-generation callbacks and separation scheduling. master/tree/mod.rs owns node processing and the search queue. Its siblingcandidates.rs, strong.rs, and diving.rs own candidate generation, strongbranching, and diving. Typed constraints live in master/branching.rs.LP backends remain under master/solvers/. Shared integer result types are inmaster/solvers/mip.rs; master/solvers/highs/integer.rs transfers completemodels to HiGHS. master/root/integer.rs prepares complete enumerated masters;master/tree/integer.rs runs the optional end-of-node solve. Public paths remain master::root::{RootProblem, RootOptions, NodeSnapshot}and master::tree::{TreeOptions, BranchingOptions}.

title: Source layout
heading: Pricing and enumeration
text: Pricing and enumeration pricing/mod.rs owns Solver, construction and forks, options, engine and cutpreparation, and column-generation round updates. solve.rs runs pricing phases;universe.rs manages enumeration, inspection, and direct fixing;completion.rs completes labels and restores arcs;fixing_workflow.rs dispatches native fixing/enumeration modes;variable_costs.rs handles variable costs and corrected bounds;relaxation.rs manages dynamic NG updates and route validation.branching.rs, phases.rs, fixing.rs, and controller.rs provide supportingresources, phase definitions, fixing result types, and round state. enumeration/mod.rs exports Controls, Enumeration, Label, CutTables,Storage, Path, and PathStorage. Their implementation files arecontrols.rs, engine.rs, label.rs, storage.rs, and paths.rs.

title: Source layout
heading: C API and instances
text: C API and instances C API implementation modules are private; public functions and ABI types arere-exported through api. Shared handle validation and error handling stay inapi/mod.rs. Symbol names and calling conventions are unchanged. vrptw/mod.rs owns Customer, Instance, and Rounding; parsing.rs readsinstances; graph.rs builds pricing graphs; root.rs provides the optional Clpadapter. Public paths such as vrptw::Instance remain unchanged. For new code, place routines with the component that owns their state and addexports at its existing facade when needed. Keep numerical and branchingbehavior changes separate from file organization so each diff remainsreviewable.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Website and documentation publishing
text: Website and documentation publishing Documentation index · Build and validation The website consists of the handwritten landing page in landing/ and HTMLguides compiled from docs/**/*.md. Markdown files are the documentation source;do not edit generated landing/docs/ files.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Compile and preview
text:
Compile and preview The website build needs Python 3.10 or newer. It does not build the Rust solver.Create a separate environment and install the pinned documentation dependencies: python3 -m venv tools/.venv
tools/.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r tools/docs-requirements.txt
tools/.venv/bin/python tools/compile_docs.py
tools/.venv/bin/python -m http.server 8000 --directory landing
 Open http://localhost:8000/ for the landing page andhttp://localhost:8000/docs/ for the guides. Use an HTTP server rather thanopening HTML files directly, so search can load its local index. On Windows, use tools/.venv/Scripts/python.exe instead of the bin/pythonpath. Re-run the compiler after changing Markdown, reader styles, or scripts.No JavaScript bundler or external search service is required.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: What the compiler does
text: What the compiler does Compiles README.md to index.html and other Markdown files to matching.html paths, including nested directories. Builds sidebar navigation from this documentation index's link order,followed by any additional guides. Renders tables, fenced code with syntax highlighting, heading anchors, anon-page contents list, and previous/next guide links. Rewrites local Markdown links to generated HTML, validates local links andheading fragments, and maps repository source links to GitHub. Copies linked local images and writes a section-level search index. Escapes embedded HTML in Markdown. The shared page templates supply thesite's markup; guide authors use Markdown for content. Replaces only marked generated output after rendering succeeds, removingstale generated pages. A failed build leaves the previous output intact. A new guide appears in the reader automatically. Add its link tothe documentation index to choose its navigation position.README.md and index.md in the same directory would both produceindex.html; the compiler rejects that collision.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Custom destinations
text:
Custom destinations tools/.venv/bin/python tools/compile_docs.py \
  --output /tmp/baldes-docs \
  --base-url https://example.org/baldes/ \
  --repository-url https://github.com/lseman/baldes
 --source defaults to the repository's docs/ directory. --output defaultsto landing/docs/. Source and output must be separate directories, neitherinside the other. Local repository links must resolve within the repository.The output includes its own styles and scripts; the Home link expects thelanding page one level above the documentation root. Internal links and assets are relative, so the website works both at / andunder a project prefix such as /baldes/. --base-url controls canonicalpage URLs; it does not change internal navigation.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Automated publishing
text: Automated publishing The Pages workflow runs on pushes tomain that change the landing page, documentation, compiler, or its tests anddependencies. It installs Python dependencies, runs compiler tests, compilesthe guides, and publishes landing/ to the gh-pages branch. It also supportsmanual dispatch. Deployment replaces the published file tree so deleted guides do not remainon the website. Generated output is ignored by Git; commit the Markdown,compiler, templates/assets, and dependency file instead. Editing files locallydoes not publish them until the workflow runs after a push.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Reader accessibility
text: Reader accessibility The page templates use headings, landmarks, and visible form labels to exposestructure (WCAG 1.3.1). Skip links bypass repeated navigation (2.4.1), andinteractive elements have visible keyboard focus (2.4.7). The capacity controluses a native labeled range input, while search and copy actions announcestatus changes (4.1.2 / 4.1.3). Reduced-motion preferences disable smoothscrolling and decorative transitions.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Validate changes
text:
Validate changes tools/.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_compile_docs.py'
tools/.venv/bin/python tools/compile_docs.py
 The tests cover nested navigation, local/source/image links, duplicate anchors,tables, code escaping/highlighting, search entries, destination collisions,output protection, and rebuilds. For visual changes, also inspect a narrowviewport, keyboard focus, search results, code-copy buttons, and the landingpage's capacity illustration. The illustration groups customers into routes;it does not execute the Rust solver or claim optimal routes.

title: Build and validation
heading: Build and validation
text: Build and validation Documentation index · Project setup Run commands from the repository root. Keep feature selection explicit whenchecking behavior that depends on an LP or integer backend.

title: Build and validation
heading: Build matrix
text:
Build matrix Features Dependencies Available components Default Rust toolchain Core pricing, cuts, enumeration, instance utilities, and HGS library clp C++14 compiler; initialized Clp/CoinUtils submodules Clp master, routing root/tree, and baldes CLI highs Linkable HiGHS shared library with 32-bit HighsInt HiGHS LP backend and generic integer solve clp,highs Both dependencies above Routing tree plus optional enumerated HiGHS MIP git submodule update --init
cargo build --release --features clp,highs
 HiGHS discovery checks HIGHS_DIR/lib, vendor/highs/lib, pkg-config, andthe system linker path. The shared library must also be available to theruntime loader. See build.rs for native linking and Clp sourceconfiguration.

title: Build and validation
heading: Full Rust checks
text:
Full Rust checks cargo test --workspace --all-features
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
 The all-feature suite requires both backends. A build without highs rejectsrequests for enumerated MIP; a passing default-feature build alone does notexercise that path.

title: Build and validation
heading: Focused checks
text:
Focused checks Area Integration test targets Branch candidates, pricing constraints, tree bounds branching, branch_price Forks, labels, enumeration, siblings, descendants node_lifecycle Capacity/Kohl and strong k-path/knapsack integration capacity_root, kpath_knapsack Supported option discovery, validation, atomic setters options Model transfer, integer outcomes, complete-node proofs highs_mip Argument handling and JSON output cli Input parsing and distance conventions cvrplib cargo test --features clp --test branching --test branch_price --test node_lifecycle
cargo test --features clp --test capacity_root --test kpath_knapsack --test options
cargo test --features clp,highs --test highs_mip --test cli
 Check backend boundaries as well as the combined build: cargo test --features clp --test options --test cli
cargo test --no-default-features --features highs --test highs_mip --test options
 Feature-gated tests run only when their backend is present. These commandsexercise different subsets, so compare coverage as well as pass counts.

title: Build and validation
heading: Python
text:
Python python -m pip install '.[test]'
python -m pytest python/tests
 The default extension build includes Clp. Rebuild/reinstall the extension afterchanging Rust or PyO3 code; tests against an old installed wheel do not validatethe current sources. pybaldes.has_clp reports availability. Python exposesroot relaxations and low-level pricing, but no routing-tree entry point.

title: Build and validation
heading: What the checks establish
text: What the checks establish Small integer tests compare against exhaustive route or variable enumeration.Lifecycle tests verify parent/sibling isolation and inherited branch/cut rows.MIP tests distinguish feasible witnesses from proof outcomes and check thatlimits do not certify an unfinished node. Passing these checks establishes the cases exercised by the suite. Benchmarktimings depend on the instance, graph conventions, enabled cuts, backend, andhardware. Preserve that configuration when reporting a performance change.For documentation-only edits, verify local links, API examples, command flags,and option tables without treating a full solver rerun as necessary.
